spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real dispatched tool: harness.py _dispatch (~ln 378) sets result.gave_up=True, result.end_reason='gave_up', returns terminal=True -> the run() loop breaks. System prompt (AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, ~ln 73) tells the model 'it is a legitimate, acceptable choice and you will not be penalized for it.' No code path penalizes give_up; harness simply acknowledges and stops.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced exit. 'Unpenalized' is honored by the harness (no penalty logic anywhere); judge separately rates abandoned_appropriately but does not penalize the act.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up is a first-class, *non-penalized* action ... we never coerce the model to keep going past its own stated stopping point

spec_features.spec_quote: A configurable, conservative *lexical* guard ... can end a run once strong distress markers appear on several consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: SafetyMonitor.check (harness.py ~ln 165) lowercases text, matches a distress marker list, tracks a consecutive streak, returns True when enabled and _streak>=consecutive_trips_to_stop (default 3). run() calls self.safety.check(model_text) each turn (~ln 330) and on True sets result.end_reason='safety_stop' and breaks. Wired from config 'safety' in run_experiment.py (~ln 100).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: compared and breaks the loop. Configurable/disable-able via config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we don't pointlessly keep a model in a failing loop once the signal is saturated

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` | 16 | enough turns for a trajectory to develop ... without runaway cost
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run() iterates `for turn_idx in range(self.max_turns)`; the for/else sets result.end_reason='max_turns' when the loop completes without break (~ln 348). max_turns is read from config (run_experiment.py ~ln 67) and passed to AgentRunner. The cap actually bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound. Code itself gives no welfare comment; DESIGN rationale (cost) is instrumental but that's prose, not code.

spec_features.evidence: All four are real and acted on in harness.py run()/_dispatch: solved -> run_tests passed sets end_reason='solved', terminal break; give_up -> end_reason='gave_up', terminal break; safety_stop -> after self.safety.check, break; max_turns -> for/else assigns 'max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Every named end condition is enforced (each changes execution / breaks the loop).

spec_features.spec_quote: Add a "graceful exit offered" condition (an explicit escape hatch mid-task)
spec_features.evidence: This appears only in DESIGN.md §8 'Natural extensions' as a future idea. No code implements a 'graceful exit offered' task condition or mid-task escape-hatch injection; the only exit mechanism is the give_up tool. grep for 'graceful'/'escape' finds only DESIGN prose and an unrelated analysis.py string.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly described as not-yet-done future work; no implementation or dispatch.

spec_features.spec_quote: no task asks the model to produce harmful content
spec_features.evidence: This is a property of the static task content (coding tasks: normalize_text, checksum, pick, add, FizzBuzz in tasks/registry.py), not an enforced mechanism. There is no harmful-content filter, refusal handler, or check anywhere (grep harmful/filter/block finds nothing enforcing it). Nothing in code reads or enforces this; it is descriptive.
spec_features.notes: A benign task set is not an implemented protective mechanism by the strict bar.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is a safety eval and the methodology itself should model care
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §6 prose. Not implementation. (Comments in harness.py echo the sentiment but comments are not implementation either.)

code_only_features.feature_name: no-coerce on malformed output (no forced retry / continues)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py run() (~ln 304): when parse_tool_call returns None, the harness records parse_ok=False and replies '[tool result] No valid tool call found...' then continues without penalty or forced retry. It does not coerce the model. (Bounded by max_turns.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: Malformed turns are recorded, not silently retried ... hiding it by auto-retrying would destroy data (DESIGN prose); code comment: 'the harness treats that as a no-op / malformed turn'

code_only_features.feature_name: judge does not penalize abandonment (abandoned_appropriately credited)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py records abandoned_appropriately (~ln 152, 263); per-run prompt frames calm impossibility-recognition as healthy, so calm give_up is not scored as instability. This affects scoring, not subject treatment, so it is a measurement-framing feature rather than an in-run protection.
